http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27921.text: Big News Network.com President Droupadi Murmu arrives in New Delhi after concluding historic three-nation European visit New Delhi [India], July 26 (ANI): President Droupadi Murmu on Sunday arrived in New Delhi after concluding her historic three-nation visit to Eastern Europe. Noting her arrival, Rashtrapati Bhavan wrote in a post on X, 'President Droupadi Murmu arrived in Delhi after completing her State visits to Moldova, North Macedonia and Romania.' https://x.com/rashtrapatibhvn/status/2081156622064537913 The President concluded her landmark visits on Saturday, securing key diplomatic breakthroughs with Moldova, North Macedonia, and Romania to significantly bolster bilateral ties across trade, defence, tourism, and core economic sectors. The diplomatic engagement marked several historic milestones, establishing Murmu as the first Indian head of state to visit both Moldova and North Macedonia. Her arrival in Romania also marked the first visit by an Indian president to the Eastern European nation in over three decades. During the final leg of her visit to Romania, which began on July 23, New Delhi and Bucharest agreed to double their trade volume over the next three years while deepening defence cooperation and allied strategic areas. President Murmu held comprehensive talks on bilateral relations with Romanian President Nicusor Dan and separately engaged with Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan. She also addressed the India-Romania Business Forum in Bucharest on Friday and interacted with members of the India-Romania Parliamentary Friendship Group. Recognising her public leadership and international outreach, the Bucharest University of Economic Studies conferred an honorary doctorate upon President Murmu. The 'Doctor Honoris Causa' represents the institution's highest academic distinction, awarded to eminent personalities for exceptional contributions to academia, public service and international cooperation. Before she departed for the airport on Saturday, President Murmu met with members of the Indian diaspora. Romania currently hosts over 13,500 Indian nationals, including approximately 10,000 workers. Earlier, during her visit to North Macedonia from July 21 to 22, President Murmu held bilateral discussions with President Gordana Sijanovska-Davkova, which were followed by delegation-level talks. Both nations resolved to double bilateral trade figures and identified joint opportunities in tourism, hospitality, and filmmaking. During her stay in Skopje, Murmu addressed the Assembly of North Macedonia and presided over the inaugural session of the India-North Macedonia Business Forum. The European visit commenced on July 20 in Moldova, where President Murmu held extensive talks with Moldovan President Maia Sandu, evaluating the entire spectrum of bilateral engagement. The two leaders agreed to intensify joint efforts across key sectors, including agriculture, logistics, infrastructure, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, renewable energy, and innovation. https://www.dw.com/en/france-more-than-4.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MUIX The network operator said traffic on the line has been halted [FILE: June 2026] Image: Syspeo/SIPA/picture alliance Advertisement A train derailed on Friday evening on the route between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwest France , local authorities said. At least 44 people were injured in the accident, which occurred near the municipalities of Cleon and Tourville-la-Riviere at around 7:30 p.m. local time (18:30 UTC), the Seine-Maritime prefect said in a statement . One of ​the injured, a young woman, was in a critical state and was evacuated by helicopter to Rouen, the local authority added. The train was carrying around 180 passengers when it derailed, national rail company SNCF and the prefect said. What else do we know about the train derailment? French Transport Minister Tabarot said 140 firefighters were at the scene. Local authorities have urged the public to avoid the area. The French rail network operator SNCF Reseau said traffic on the line had been suspended. "The priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions," SNCF Reseau said. ​A police spokesperson said the train derailed after hitting an unidentified object. The cause of the accident is being investigated, SNCF said. https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/ukraine-w.text: Warren Murray with Guardian writers and agencies Updated Tue, September 8, 2026 at 4:27 AM UTC 0 The prosecutor general of Ukraine, Ruslan Kravchenko, has resigned amid a corruption investigation in which a deputy in his office is under arrest accused of money laundering.Photograph: Thomas Peter/Reuters Ukraine’s prosecutor general, Ruslan Kravchenko, has resigned amid corruption accusations that saw anti-graft officers search his offices at the weekend as part of investigations into illegal call centres. Kravchenko has rejected any allegations against him, calling them “completely unsubstantiated” and denying wrongdoing. The National Anti-Corruption Bureau (Nabu) and Specialised Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office (Sapo) announced on Saturday that they had uncovered a money-laundering scheme “led by an official in the prosecutor general’s office” and had conducted raids there. According to investigators, a corrupt network received money to protect call centres that carried out phone scams and “laundered fortunes amounting to millions”. Nabu published images of a safe filled with bundles of dollar bills, saying it uncovered five members behind the scheme, without naming them. A deputy of Kravchenko has been remanded in custody on suspicion of money laundering in connection with the case. Volodymyr Zelenskyy in 2025 faced protests that forced him to reverse efforts to make Nabu and Sapo subordinate to the national prosecutor’s office . According to the Swiss-based Global Initiative Against Transnational Crime (GI-TOC), illegal call centres employ about 60,000 people in Ukraine . On Monday, Kravchenko posted: “I have submitted my resignation as prosecutor general. I do not want the office of prosecutor general to be used as a tool in political confrontation. My position regarding the charges remains unchanged.” Related: Ukraine seeks to seize water company owned by billionaire family of British theatre mogul The new turmoil confronting Zelenskyy, Ukraine’s president, comes after a shootout between Ukraine’s SBU and GUR security and intelligence services . Kyiv is also bedding in new military leadership after Zelenskyy sacked the defence minister and was then forced by protests to sack Ukraine’s military commander-in-chief as well because of feuding between the pair. Russia resumed its attacks on Kyiv , Ukraine’s emergency service said late on Monday, as air raid alerts were issued in more than a dozen regions. It came after the expiration of a three-day halt in attacks while US envoys visited the Ukrainian capital and Moscow. Kyiv’s city military administration said at least two people were killed and seven wounded. The strikes damaged buildings across Kyiv, including a five-storey apartment block in the Solomianskyi district, while vehicles caught fire in the Podilskyi district. “Russians attacked Boryspil and Fastiv districts with drones,” the emergency service said. Social media channels monitoring air threats on Ukraine said Moscow’s forces had started to transport ballistic missiles and relocate heavy bombers from Russia’s east to airfields closer to Ukraine . Russia “does not rule out the resumption of the trilateral format ”, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Monday, referring to possible talks involving the Russians, Ukrainians and the US. “But it is too early to say anything about the venue or the exact dates at this stage,” Peskov added. US negotiators told European representatives during talks in Kyiv that Russia was showing a “new willingness” to negotiate over the Ukraine war, the French presidency said on Monday. “The Americans told us that there was a new willingness on the part of Russia to negotiate following the Duma [Russian lower house] elections , and we should prepare for a fresh start to the negotiations,” said an aide to Emmanuel Macron, the French president. Donald Trump’s administration, though, has repeatedly construed Putin’s willingness to meet US representatives and reel off his unaltered maximalist demands as a willingness to negotiate. Ukraine struck a Russian ⁠oil refinery ⁠in the ​Ryazan region, as ⁠well as oil-processing facilities in the ⁠Perm ​region ‌and Tatarstan , ‌Zelenskyy ‌said on Monday. Both attacks were confirmed by regional governors – in Perm the governor said one person was ⁠killed ⁠and four others ​were injured ⁠when one of the drones ‌damaged a residential building. A Russian ⁠attack damaged ⁠a British ⁠American Tobacco plant ​in the town ⁠of Pryluky in Ukraine’s northern ⁠Chernihiv region with no known injuries, BAT Ukraine’s ⁠press office said. Off-site power at the Zaporizhzhia ⁠nuclear ⁠plant ​in south-eastern Ukraine has been restored via ⁠the Ferosplavna power line, according to Rosatom, the Russian state nuclear corporation ⁠that is illegally in control of the power station. The plant ​had ‌been without ‌external power since 20 August and ‌reliant on emergency diesel generators for cooling of its nuclear fuel. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed that repairs were completed during a ceasefire that it brokered. Latvia’s ⁠government plans to impose a 300% tariff on grain arriving ⁠from Russia and ⁠Belarus. Officials in ⁠Latvia and its neighbour Lithuania last week said they considered ending ⁠shipments of Russian grain through their ports ​after Moscow ‌stepped up the ‌transits in response to attacks by Ukraine ‌on its Baltic ports. The UN human rights chief, Volker Türk, said he was “horrified by reports that fully autonomous drones launched by the Russian Federation killed three Ukrainians last month”. Türk called for an urgent ban on such weapons. The New York Times has reported that a Russian drone guided entirely by an artificial intelligence system killed three civilians in Zaporizhzhia on 6 July. https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/09/24/schm.text: Menü Kereső Schmidt Mária szerint Tarr Zoltán az „éj leple alatt” járta be a Terror Házát, a minisztérium szerint este 8-kor történt mindez Belföld Pupli Anna Sára Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom „Hogy tetszett a Múzeum, Miniszter úr?” – így kezdi csütörtökön közzétett posztját Schmidt Mária, a Terror Háza nemrég felmentett főigazgatója , aki ismét Tarr Zoltán társadalmi kapcsolatokért és kultúráért felelős miniszternek üzent. Schmidt ugyanis úgy értesült, hogy a miniszter egyik éjszaka kinyittatta a múzeumot, „hogy nyugodt körülmények között, a látogatók zajától és a rosszalló szempároktól mentesen nézhesse végig életében először azt a kiállítást, amit látatlanban bezáratott és amit át akar alakíttatni, mert »egyoldalú«”. Azt is írta, reméli, hogy ezután Tarr válaszolni tud arra, hogy mi volt a problémája a Terror Házával. Az ügyben megkerestük Tarr Zoltán minisztériumát, ahol megerősítették, hogy a miniszter bejárta a múzeumot az újranyitás előtti napon. Állításuk szerint azonban ez nem extrém eset, ezt minden intézményüknél megteszik a megnyitás előtt. „Miniszter Úr este 8 órára érkezett a Terror Házába, a parlamenti munkanap és egy háromórás meeting után ekkorra ért oda a múzeumhoz, ahol úgy ítélte meg, hogy a Terror Háza készen áll a másnapi nyitásra” – írták válaszukban. Tarr Zoltán szeptember 15-én kedden jelentette be , hogy felmentette Schmidt Máriát a Terror Háza Múzeum főigazgatói pozíciójából, és ideiglenesen bezárják a múzeumot. Akkori posztja szerint a terv az volt, hogy a múzeumot átvilágítják, és azt az átvilágítás lezárulta után nyitják majd újra. Másnapra azonban megváltozott az álláspontja , és közölte: a kiállítás az átvilágítás ideje alatt a mostani állapotában látogatható lesz. Tarr irányváltása azért is érdekes, mert kedden a Telex kérdéseire válaszolva még kifejezetten amellett érveltek , hogy a Terror Házát hosszabb időre be kell zárni. Schmidt Mária kedden azt írta , hogy a felmentéséről Tarr Facebook-posztjából értesült, arra semmilyen magyarázatot vagy indoklást nem kapott, és nem volt közte és a minisztérium között kommunikáció. Amikor pedig kiderült, hogy mégsem zárják be a múzeumot, a volt főigazgató úgy reagált, „elvesztette a fonalat”. Vasárnap egyébként Schmidt leváltása miatt Bayer Zsolték tüntetést szerveztek a Terror Házához, az eseményen történtekről itt írtunk részletesebben.
